name: Incline Barbell Guillotine Press
description: The incline guillotine press is a barbell pressing variation performed on an incline bench where the bar is lowered toward the neck and upper chest rather than the mid-chest. This extreme stretch position maximally loads the clavicular head of the pectoralis major under a wide grip. Due to the high shoulder stress in this position, it is considered a high-risk exercise requiring significant shoulder health and experience.

execution.starting_position: Set an adjustable bench to a 30–45 degree incline and position it inside a power rack. Lie back and grip the barbell with a wide pronated grip, slightly wider than shoulder width.
execution.setup_instructions: Set the safety catches at an appropriate height. The bar path target is the neck and clavicle area, so ensure the spotter or safety pins are positioned accordingly.
steps: Step 1: Unrack the bar with arms extended, holding it above the upper chest and clavicle area.
Step 2: Lower the bar slowly toward the neck and upper chest (clavicle region), maintaining control throughout the descent.
Step 3: Touch or come very close to the clavicle/upper chest area without bouncing.
Step 4: Press the bar back to the starting position by driving through the chest and triceps.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale during the controlled descent to the neck. Exhale powerfully during the press upward.
common_mistakes: Using excessive weight — this is a stretch-focused exercise requiring relatively light loads
Lowering too fast, losing control at the bottom
Performing with shoulder impingement or prior shoulder injuries
safety_considerations: HIGH RISK: This exercise places the shoulder in an extreme externally rotated, horizontally abducted position under load — not recommended for beginners or those with shoulder pathology
Always use safety pins or a spotter
Start with an empty bar or very light weight to assess shoulder tolerance
If any shoulder pain is felt, stop immediately
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Lower bar to clavicle or neck level only if shoulder health permits. Partial range may be appropriate for most trainees.
coaching_cues: Wide grip, elbows flared — this is intentional for upper pec targeting
Control the descent — do not drop the bar toward the neck
